glosses: to embarrass, to confound, to abash

examples.translation: You don't have anything to be ashamed of.
examples.english: You don't have anything to be ashamed of.

examples.text: Odniósł jak najlepsze wrażenie i wcale nie żenował się wyrazić żal, że...
examples.translation: He got the best possible impression and was not embarrassed at all to express regret that...
examples.english: He got the best possible impression and was not embarrassed at all to express regret that...

examples.text: ...żenował się tym traumatycznym doświadczeniem tak dalece, że poszedł na współpracę z bezpieką, byleby nie ujawniono tych – wstydliwych dlań ‐ okoliczności.
examples.translation: ... he was embarrassed by this traumatic experience to such an extent that he went to work with the Communist secret police, so long as these circumstances, shameful to him, were not revealed.

glosses: sprawiać, że ktoś czuje się zakłopotany

examples.text: Nie przeszkadza mi, jeśli ktoś zaklnie na meczu, ale żenuje, gdy inwektywy padają w stronę sędziego.

glosses: to humiliate; to disrupt somebody's composure or comfort with acting publicly or freely; to abash.

examples.text: The crowd's laughter and jeers embarrassed him.

glosses: To hinder from liberty of movement; to impede; to obstruct.

examples.text: The motion was advanced in order to embarrass the progress of the bill.
If they [registers] act It all, it must be by opposing their flat surfaces to the current of rising smoke in a manner which cannot fail to embarrass and impede its motion..

This will... be the principal part of education; and this alone will effectively dispel that theological philosophy, which, in its decline, is still powerful enough to embarrass the course both of intellectual and social progress.

In the case at bar, there is very little beyond bare assertions and bald statements against the unidentified and unspecified Defendant(s). The claim is vexatious in that the Defendant, if identifiable, is left both embarrassed and unable to defend itself. The Court is left with a proceeding so ill-defined that it is unable to discern an argument, or identify any specific material facts.

glosses: To involve in difficulties concerning money matters; to encumber with debt; to beset with urgent claims or demands.

examples.text: A man or his business is embarrassed when he cannot meet his pecuniary engagements.

glosses: To perplex mentally; confuse, disconcert; catch off guard.

examples.text: Obyczaje cywilizacji wykazują pewną trwałość i Niemcy w okupowanej zachodniej Europie najwyraźniej się żenowali, nie ujawniając swoich celów, natomiast w Polsce występowali zupełnie otwarcie.
